_readme: Edit this file each offseason instead of touching scripts/fetch-rosters.mjs.

You normally shouldn't need to edit it by hand at all: the Admin tab on myffl.html (visible once logged in) edits this same file and commits it, validated by api/save-leagues.js. Hand-editing still works and is the fallback if that endpoint is misconfigured.
Any field added here that the Admin tab doesn't know about is preserved untouched when it saves, so adding one by hand is safe — but do teach the tab about it if it's meant to be editable.
provider: 'mfl' (default if omitted), 'espn', or 'sleeper' — which fetch logic/auth to use. Sleeper needs no auth at all.
id: the league ID for the current year (find it in the league's URL).

franchiseId: your team ID within that league (MFL: 4-digit franchise ID; ESPN: numeric team ID; Sleeper: numeric roster_id, found by matching your username against /v1/league/<id>/users + /v1/league/<id>/rosters).

name: optional fallback display name, used only if the live league/team name can't be fetched. Not editable from the Admin tab, which shows the live name from the last sync instead — editing this changed nothing visible, so the control was removed rather than left looking meaningful. A league added from the Admin tab has no name until its first sync.

type: 'dynasty', 'salarycap', 'draftonly', or 'redraft' — controls which top-level sub-tab a league appears under, in that order. Mostly a display concern, with one exception: 'salarycap' is what adds the Salary/Yrs columns and the cap summary to a card, and what makes the sync fetch the salary cap and salary adjustments at all.

NOTE: 'draftonly' is the type formerly called 'bestball'. Best Ball is a scoring system, not a league type — several salary-cap leagues use best-ball scoring — so it lives in tags now and never appears as a type.

NOTE: there was also a 'format' field ('dynasty' or 'auction'). It is gone. 'auction' always agreed exactly with type 'salarycap', which now drives that behaviour alone, and 'dynasty' was never read by anything. api/save-leagues.js strips the key on save, so it will not come back.

NOTE: with rankingType unset (the normal case) the ranking set follows the NFL calendar by itself — ROS from kickoff through the Super Bowl, then DYNASTY for 'dynasty' leagues and DRAFT for everything else until the next kickoff. Both boundaries are computed (kickoff = the Thursday after Labor Day; Super Bowl = the second Sunday in February), so nothing has to be switched over by hand each year. 'salarycap' leagues sit with draftonly and redraft on DRAFT rather than DYNASTY — deliberate, despite their contracts and taxi squads, because they're managed on a redraft cadence (cap resets, annual re-auction). Pin rankingType on an individual league if one ever needs to differ.
ESPN leagues additionally require ESPN_S2 and ESPN_SWID GitHub Actions secrets (browser cookies, not a login).

Array order is display order everywhere on the page (Rosters, Standings, Scoring) — including the header's quick-link toolbar, which uses this same order with Draft Only leagues filtered out. There's no separate ordering for the toolbar.

nickname: optional short label for that toolbar — it has room for about one line of short labels, not full league names. Blank falls back to the live league name (leagueDisplayName). Editable from the Admin tab, right alongside the league's other fields.

lineupPilot: MFL, Sleeper, or ESPN. When true, the sync also fetches this week's starters (MFL via TYPE=liveScoring, Sleeper via its matchups endpoint, ESPN via view=mRoster scoped to the current scoring period) and the Rosters card shows a checkbox editor instead of the plain Active Roster table. On MFL it's a real editor (login required to actually submit); Sleeper's public API has no write endpoint at all and ESPN's isn't wired up here, so both render permanently read-only regardless of login — checkboxes shown for reference only, no Save button ever. Set on every league that requires a submitted starting lineup.

tags: optional array of extra badge labels shown in the card's upper-right corner (e.g. 'Superflex') — anything not already derivable from type. The type badge (Dynasty/Salary Cap/Draft Only/Redraft) is added automatically, no need to repeat it here. 'Best Ball' is a legitimate tag: it's a scoring system, not a league type. A 'Superflex' tag also switches that league's FantasyPros rankings to their superflex (OP) list.

rankingType: optional FantasyPros ranking set behind the ECR column. Normally leave it unset: it then follows the season on its own, per the NOTE above. Setting it to DYNASTY, DRAFT, ROS, WEEKLY or ADP is the manual override — it pins that league to that one set year-round and opts it out of the seasonal flip entirely. The Admin tab's Rankings dropdown is this same choice, with 'Automatic' meaning unset. Needs a FANTASYPROS_API_KEY secret — without one the ECR column is simply blank and nothing else changes.

scoring: optional FantasyPros scoring format for the ECR column — 'PPR', 'HALF', or 'STD'. Normally leave it blank: the sync reads each league's own settings and works out which list applies from what a reception is worth there (1 = PPR, 0.5 = HALF, 0 or no rule = STD), so this never has to be transcribed from a rules document. A league whose rate is none of those three is left alone rather than rounded to the nearest. Setting it explicitly pins the league. NOTE: blank used to mean PPR; it now means 'detect it', so pin PPR explicitly if that is what you want.

season: optional four-digit year pinning which season this league is read from. Normally leave it blank: the sync resolves a season per league and only moves to a new one once that league actually exists there, so leagues whose commissioners roll over in February and in April are both handled without a config edit. A league whose new site isn't up yet falls back to the season it actually last played rather than showing an empty one. Recorded back into data/rosters.json per league, which is how the next sync knows a league has already rolled over. Sleeper is the exception — a new season is a new league id there, so update the id instead. Setting this pins the league and skips the check entirely.

startYear: optional four-digit year, the earliest season that's actually yours in this league. A league's own history usually predates a manager joining it — the franchise id league.results[] is keyed to (league.franchiseId) belonged to somebody else before then, so a pre-join year's finish, weekly high, or season high is a real answer about the wrong person, not a gap to fill in. Blank (the normal state) means the whole known history is yours. Set from the Admin tab, it excludes any year before it from the History tab's Results and Finances cards (see isBeforeStartYear in myffl.html) and also keeps the history/scoring backfills (fetch-rosters.mjs) from spending MFL/ESPN requests fetching a year nobody will ever see.

historyLeagueIds: optional object mapping a four-digit year to the MFL league ID that season actually used — {"2010": "34034", ...}. MFL only, and only needed when TYPE=league's own history.league[] chain (what the history backfill normally walks automatically — see fetchMflLeagueHistory in scripts/lib/providers.mjs) is wrong or missing for that year. Confirmed real for Survivor (id 23545): its own chain self-lists "2015: id=23545", but querying that id for 2015 returns zero standings rows and an auth error on every playoffBracket call, while the real 2015 season (12 teams, real brackets) lives under a completely different id (39564) the chain never mentions — and 39564's own history.league[] is empty, so there's no automatic way to walk further back from it either. There's no Admin tab field for this — it's rare and specific enough per-league that a form wouldn't earn its keep, so it's hand-edited directly (still validated server-side in api/save-leagues.js so a malformed edit fails loudly). An entry here WINS outright over whatever the automatic chain says for that year, even if the chain already lists something — see applyHistoryLeagueIdOverrides in fetch-rosters.mjs.

commishContact: optional commissioner contact for salary-cap leagues — where the Rosters card's contract-length summary goes. Only salary-cap leagues generate that summary, so it is ignored elsewhere and the Admin tab only offers the field for them. An email address opens a pre-filled mailto:; anything starting with http://, https://, or slack:// is opened as a link instead (there's no plan to pre-fill into it), for a commissioner who'd rather be reached some other way — e.g. a Discord invite, or a slack://channel?team=TEAM_ID&id=USER_ID deep link straight to their DM (that's the real Slack URI scheme; there is no separate slack://user form). NOTE: this field was renamed from commishEmail, which only ever accepted an email address; api/save-leagues.js strips the old key on save.

rulesUrl: optional link to the league's actual rules page/doc. When set, shows a small 📝 icon next to the league name on the Rosters, Standings, and Scoring cards, opening it in a new tab. Omitted entirely for leagues without one.

cutdownRosterSize: optional integer, Dynasty leagues only — the regular-season roster size the league's own rules require, driving the Rosters card's cut-planning dropdown and its 'N/M cuts planned' banner. Deliberately NOT the same number as MFL's own rosterLimits.size (TYPE=league): a Dynasty commissioner routinely raises that limit for the offseason so a roster swollen with rookie picks doesn't get flagged on MFL's own site, so it describes what MFL will currently tolerate, not what the league's rules actually require once the season starts. No provider exposes the real number, so it's set by hand from each league's own rules document and stays static year to year unless the league votes to change it. Without it the cut-planning dropdown still renders (still useful to pre-mark candidates) but the banner has no target to count against and stays hidden.

dues: optional dollar amount, the league's flat entry fee. Assumed the same every season, so this is one number rather than one per year — set by hand from each league's own rules, like cutdownRosterSize above, and editable from the Admin tab. Feeds the History tab's Finances card (the Dues column). Left blank, it's treated as $0 rather than unknown — see payout1/2/3 below for why this card defaults an unentered amount to zero rather than leaving it blank.

payout1 / payout2 / payout3: optional dollar amounts — what the league actually pays out for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place. Assumed constant every season like dues above, and every league here is assumed to pay exactly the top 3; there's no field for 4th place or below. The Finances card's Won column looks a franchise's Finish for a given year (from the Results card's own backfilled league.results) up against these three fields. Unlike most of this file's optional fields, an unset amount here reads as $0 rather than unknown: a Finish outside the top 3 is a real, known $0 given the top-3-only assumption, and a league that simply hasn't entered its payouts yet nets to $0 rather than leaving the Total column blank — the whole point of the card is a Total that goes negative the moment a real entry fee outweighs whatever was won. Editable from the Admin tab.

payoutDivisionWinner: optional dollar amount, independent of final placement — for the best REGULAR-SEASON record, not whoever actually won the bracket (those two routinely differ: a team can enter the playoffs as the top seed and still lose the final, or vice versa — see computeMflSeasonPlacements' own header in scripts/lib/history.mjs). The Finances card pays it when league.franchiseId matches that year's league.results[].divisionWinnerFranchiseId. Unlike payoutWeeklyHigh/payoutSeasonHigh below, that field is NOT a separate on-demand backfill — it's stamped by the same placement backfill that fills rank/total/guessed (mflDivisionWinner reads MFL's regular-season standings order it already fetched for the placement walk; espnDivisionWinner reads ESPN's own playoffSeed off the same response rankCalculatedFinal comes from), so it's expected to be populated as soon as a year's Finish is, not lag behind it — the one exception is a draftonly league, which ranks by total points and never fetches head-to-head standings, so this stays unset there the same way every other placement-based field does for that type. Same $0-when-unset convention as payout1/2/3. Editable from the Admin tab.

payoutWeeklyHigh / payoutSeasonHigh: optional dollar amounts, independent of final placement (a last-place team can still have banked a weekly win). These are two DIFFERENT KINDS of award, not two versions of the same one: payoutWeeklyHigh is paid out fresh every week 1-18 — each week's own top scorer wins it again, so a single season can pay it out up to 18 times, possibly several to the same franchise — while payoutSeasonHigh is a single once-a-season award for the highest total points across weeks 1-17 only (week 18 can win the weekly award but never counts toward the season total). Same $0-when-unset convention as payout1/2/3. The Finances card sums payoutWeeklyHigh once per entry in that year's league.results[].scoring.weeklyHighs array carrying league.franchiseId, and adds payoutSeasonHigh when league.franchiseId matches scoring.seasonHigh — see leagueFinancesSummary in myffl.html, which shows the total as a click-to-reveal breakdown rather than spelling every week out inline. That `scoring` field is populated by a separate, on-demand backfill (scripts/backfill-scoring.mjs / backfill-scoring.yml) rather than the regular sync — computing it needs one MFL request per week fetched with no bulk endpoint to fetch it in one call, expensive enough that it deliberately isn't run automatically. Expect most years to show no scoring data for a while after this shipped; a year with no `scoring` yet contributes $0 here just like a league that hasn't entered the payout amount, which is indistinguishable on purpose — the year-by-year breakdown still shows real Place-based Won amounts in the meantime, it just doesn't yet know about a high-score win. Editable from the Admin tab.
